summary: Ernst Johann Eitel worked in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Evangelical Seminaries of Maulbronn and Blaubeuren, Georgii-Gymnasium, and the University of Tübingen. He served with the London Missionary Society (~1865–1879) and at the University of Adelaide (~1897–1908).

Ernst Kuhn worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin, Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, Leipzig, and Heidelberg, studying under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at Halle-Wittenberg, Leipzig, Heidelberg, and the University of Munich (1877–1917).

Ernst Leumann worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Friedrich Haag and Albrecht Weber, attending Zurich, Geneva, Leipzig, Berlin, and Strasbourg. He held posts at Oxford, Kantonsschule Frauenfeld, the University of Strasbourg, and the University of Freiburg.

Ernst Moritz Arndt worked in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Greifswald (~1791–1793) and the University of Jena (~1793–1794), later holding posts at the University of Greifswald (~1800–1811) and the University of Bonn (~1818–1860).

Ernst Osiander was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Evangelical Seminaries of Maulbronn and Blaubeuren and under Rudolf von Roth at the University of Tübingen, later serving as Repetent at Maulbronn and Blaubeuren and at Tübinger Stift.

Ernst Steinkellner works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Erich Frauwallner at the University of Vienna. His career includes posts at Vienna, the University of Pennsylvania, Kyoto University, and the Institute for Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Ernst Trumpp worked in linguistics, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Tübinger Stift under Rudolf von Roth. His career included positions at the East India Company, the University of Tübingen, and the University of Munich.

Ernst Waldschmidt was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kiel, Göttingen, and Berlin under Paul Deussen, Emil Sieg, Heinrich Lüders, August Hermann Francke, and Albert Grünwedel, later serving at Berlin and Göttingen.

Ernst Windisch worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig University under Georg Curtius, Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, Friedrich Zarncke, and Hermann Brockhaus. He held posts at Thomasschule zu Leipzig, the India Office Library, and the universities of Leipzig, Heidelberg, and Strasbourg.
Ernst Zinn was a scholar in linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Hamburg (~1947–1951), Saarland University (1951–1956), and the University of Tübingen (~1951–1978).

Erwin Rousselle worked in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Munich, Heidelberg, Freiburg, Berlin, TU Darmstadt, and Frankfurt, under Friedrich Ernst August Krause, Max Walleser, and Alexander von Staël-Holstein. He held posts at Peking, Tsinghua, Yenching, Frankfurt, and TU Darmstadt.
Esben Andreasen is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and was a visiting researcher at Otani University in 1992.

Eshin Nishimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Hanazono University, under Zenkei Shibayama, at Pendle Hill Quaker Center, and Kyoto University. He held positions at Hanazono University, Carleton College, and the Institute for Zen Studies.
Esho Kawasaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Affiliations include serving as head of the Bukkyo Bunka Kenkyujo (attested 1999) and president of the Kyushu Ryukoku Academic Society (attested 2002).

Esho Mikogami was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held appointments at Ryukoku University until 2003 (attested professor emeritus in 2007) and served as president of the Ryukoku Buddhist Society in 1997.
Esho Sasaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Affiliations include posts at Ikenobo Junior College (attested 1979) and Kyoto Women's University (attested 1991).
Esho Yamaguchi worked in Indology and philosophy. After studying at Kyoto University (~1939–1942), he held posts at Osaka University (~1969–1982) and Ritsumeikan University (~1982–1989).

Ester Bianchi is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Alfredo Cadonna and Jean-Noël Robert at Ca' Foscari University of Venice and the École Pratique des Hautes Études. She held positions at the University of Florence and University of Perugia.
Etienne Vermeersch was a philosopher who studied at Ghent University from around 1953 to 1965 and subsequently held an academic post there from 1967 to 1997.
Etsuaki Teraishi works in Indology and philosophy, with attested posts at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (1999) and the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (2001).
